title: RPG Character Builder
story: Every epic adventure begins with a character sheet. Are you a plate-armored Warrior with impossible strength? A fire-wielding Mage with arcane intelligence? A shadow-dancing Rogue with lightning reflexes? Roll your stats, pick your class, equip your gear, and watch the game calculate your HP, MP, and damage output. This is the moment before the quest begins — who will you become?
why: The RPG Character Builder synthesizes enums for class selection, structs for character state, random for stat rolling, functions for derived stat calculation, and contracts for stat boundary enforcement — a complete game-ready character creation engine.
analogy: A tabletop RPG character sheet with ERASABLE PENCIL. At session zero, you pick your class (Warrior/Mage/Rogue), roll 3d6 for each stat (strength, intelligence, agility), let the rules engine compute your derived stats (HP, MP, damage), and pick your starting gear. The sheet comes to life — every number has a reason for being there.

try_it: Add a new class like 'Paladin' (hybrid Warrior/Mage: 16 HP base, 12 MP base, damage = str*2 + intel). Add a 'level up' function that grants +1 to a chosen stat and recalculates derived stats. Add a 'reroll' feature for stats. Add a 'party' — build 3 characters and display them all side by side.
tips: 3d6 stat rolling is the classic RPG method — range 3-18, average 10-11
Derived stats should use class as a multiplier, not just addition — makes class choice meaningful
Equipment should be a tuple returned from a match on class — one lookup gives both armor and weapon
common_mistakes: Forgetting to recalculate derived stats when base stats change (level up, equipment bonuses)
Using the wrong stat for damage calculation — Warriors use STR, Mages use INT, Rogues use AGI
Stats are 3-18 from 3d6, not 1-18 — you must SUM three individual d6 rolls, not range(1,19)
